claim: Radial-glial neural stem cells (RGLs) in the dentate gyrus subregion of the hippocampus give rise to dentate granule cells and astrocytes.
source: In the adult mammalian brain, radial-glial neural stem cells (RGLs) in the dentate gyrus subregion of the hippocampus give rise to dentate granule cells and astrocytes (Seri et al., 2001; Garcia et al., 2004; Ahn and Joyner, 2005; Lagace et al., 2007; Bonaguidi et al., 2011; Encinas et al., 2011; Gonçalves et al., 2016b; Moss et al., 2016; Pilz et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research studies.

claim: Adult-born dentate granule cells integrate into hippocampal circuitry by remodeling the network and contribute to hippocampal-dependent learning and memory and regulation of emotion.
source: Adult-born dentate granule cells integrate into hippocampal circuitry by remodeling the network and ultimately contribute to hippocampal-dependent learning and memory and regulation of emotion (Gonçalves et al., 2016b; Anacker and Hen, 2017; Miller and Sahay, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Levels of adult hippocampal neurogenesis are highly sensitive to experience.
source: Levels of adult hippocampal neurogenesis are highly sensitive to experience (Cope and Gould, 2019; Vicidomini et al., 2020)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Enriching experiences (e.g., complex environments, exploration, and socialization) bias RGLs toward asymmetric divisions to generate astrocytes and neurons.
source: Whereas enriching experiences (e.g., complex environments, exploration, and socialization) bias RGLs toward asymmetric divisions to generate astrocytes and neurons (Dranovsky et al., 2011; Song et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Unfavorable conditions promote RGL quiescence (e.g., chronic stress and aging) or symmetric self-renewal to support neural stem cell expansion at the expense of neurogenesis (e.g., social isolation, seizures, and aging).
source: unfavorable conditions promote RGL quiescence (e.g., chronic stress and aging) or symmetric self-renewal to support neural stem cell (NSC) expansion at the expense of neurogenesis (e.g., social isolation, seizures, and aging) (Dranovsky et al., 2011; Sierra et al., 2015; Ibrayeva et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Asymmetric self-renewal of RGLs predominates over symmetric self-renewal division mode in the adult hippocampus.
source: Asymmetric self-renewal of RGLs predominates over symmetric self-renewal division mode in the adult hippocampus and it ensures maintenance of RGL numbers while supporting current neurogenic demands (Pilz et al., 2018; Vicidomini et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Symmetric divisions prevent premature differentiation of RGLs in a nonpermissive or unhealthy niche.
source: First, symmetric divisions prevent premature differentiation of RGLs in a nonpermissive or unhealthy niche, and consequently, avert aberrant integration of adult-born dentate granule cells detrimental to hippocampal functions (Ibrayeva et al., 2021; Cho et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: RGL amplification anticipates future demands for neurogenesis upon return to favorable conditions.
source: As such, RGL amplification anticipates future demands for neurogenesis upon return to favorable conditions.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the discussion of symmetric divisions preventing premature differentiation.

claim: Klf9 expression is elevated in quiescent RGLs compared to activated RGLs.
source: Quantification of Klf9 expression based on LacZ intensities in Klf9 LacZ/+ mice revealed enrichment in quiescent RGLs relative to activated RGLs (MCM2+) (one-way analysis of variance [ANOVA], F = 17.07, p = 0.003) (Figure 1A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing statistical significance and is illustrated in Figure 1A, B.

claim: Klf9 transcripts are significantly enriched in quiescent vs. activated (Brdu+ Nestin GFP+) RGLs.
source: Quantification of Klf9 transcripts using Image J revealed significantly enriched expression in quiescent vs. activated (Brdu+ Nestin GFP+) RGLs (Figure 1C, E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and is illustrated in Figure 1C, E.

claim: Conditional deletion of Klf9 in Gli1CreERT2-targeted adult hippocampal RGLs significantly increased the fraction of activated RGLs.
source: We found that conditional deletion of Klf9 in Gli1CreERT2-targeted adult hippocampal RGLs significantly increased the fraction of activated RGLs (% of MCM2+ tdTomato + RGLs) (Figure 1G; unpaired t-tests, Figure 1G, p < 0.0001).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing statistical significance and is illustrated in Figure 1G.

claim: Genetic overexpression of Klf9 in activated hippocampal NSCs and progenitors of adult Sox1 tTA;tet0 Klf9 mice significantly decreased the fraction of activated and dividing cells.
source: Complementing these results, we demonstrated that genetic overexpression of Klf9 in activated hippocampal NSCs and progenitors of adult Sox1 tTA;tet0 Klf9 mice (McAvoy et al., 2016; Venere et al., 2012) significantly decreased the fraction of activated and dividing cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and is illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Loss of Klf9 in RGLs results in a significantly greater fraction of multi-RGL containing clones and a smaller fraction of single RGL containing clones at 7 dpi.
source: Analysis of clonal composition at 7 dpi revealed a significantly greater fraction of multi-RGL containing clones and a smaller fraction of single RGL containing clones (Figure 2A–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 2—videos 1–8; Figure 2B, two-way ANOVA, genotype × cell type p < 0.0001, Bonferroni post hoc Klf9+/+ vs. Klf9f/f. 1 RGL n.s., 2+ RGLs p < 0.0001, 1 RGL+ p < 0.0001, no RGL n.s. Figure 2D, left panel, two-way ANOVA, genotype × cell type p < 0.0001, Bonferroni post hoc Klf9+/+ vs. Klf9f/f. 2+ RGLs p = 0.09, 2 RGLs+ P + A p < 0.0001, 2 RGLs+ p n.s. Figure 2D, right panel, two-way ANOVA, genotype × cell type p = 0.09, Bonferroni post hoc Klf9+/+ vs. Klf9f/f. 1 RGL n.s., 1 RGL+ P + A p = 0.01, 1 RGL+ P p = 0.01).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with statistical analysis and is illustrated in Figure 2A–D.

claim: Deletion of Klf9 in RGLs resulted in a significantly greater number of symmetric cell divisions compared to Klf9+/+ RGLs.
source: Deletion of Klf9 in RGLs resulted in a significantly greater number of symmetric cell divisions (39 symmetric, 38 asymmetric, 10 mice) compared to Klf9+/+ RGLs (18 symmetric, 47 asymmetric, 8 mice) (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from longitudinal two-photon imaging and is illustrated in Figure 3C.

claim: Odds of symmetric division are 2.7× higher in Gli1CreERT2:Klf9f/f:Ai14 mice compared to controls.
source: Odds of symmetric division are 2.7× higher in Gli1CreERT2:Klf9f/f:Ai14 mice, p = 0.015 likelihood-ratio test.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Klf9 functions as a brake on symmetric self-renewal of RGLs in the adult hippocampus.
source: These data provide definitive evidence for Klf9 functioning as a brake on symmetric self-renewal of RGLs in the adult hippocampus.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing increased symmetric divisions upon Klf9 deletion.

claim: Loss of Klf9 in RGLs results in downregulation of BMP4.
source: We first confirmed downregulation of Klf9 in RGLs. Next, we validated downregulation of canonical quiescence signaling factors (Bmp4) and upregulation of genes involved in lipid metabolism (Pla2g7), cell cycle (Ccn1a), mitogen signaling (epidermal growth factor receptor, Egfr), and Notch signaling (Lunatic fringe, Lfng) (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR validation data and is illustrated in Figure 4D.

claim: Loss of Klf9 in RGLs results in upregulation of genes involved in lipid metabolism (Pla2g7), cell cycle (Ccn1a), mitogen signaling (Egfr), and Notch signaling (Lfng).
source: Next, we validated downregulation of canonical quiescence signaling factors (Bmp4) and upregulation of genes involved in lipid metabolism (Pla2g7), cell cycle (Ccn1a), mitogen signaling (epidermal growth factor receptor, Egfr), and Notch signaling (Lunatic fringe, Lfng) (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR validation data and is illustrated in Figure 4D.

claim: Significantly elevated levels of NICD were observed in Gli1+ RGLs lacking Klf9.
source: Consistent with Lfng-mediated potentiation of Notch1 signaling through cleavage of the Notch1 intracellular domain (NICD), we observed significantly elevated levels of NICD in Gli1+ RGLs lacking Klf9 (Figure 4E; Hochgerner et al., 2018; Zhao and Wu, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and is illustrated in Figure 4E.

claim: High levels of Klf9 in RGLs induce BMP4 expression and repress gene modules specifying mitogen signaling, fatty acid oxidation, RGL differentiation, and cell-cycle exit to inhibit RGL expansion.
source: We infer from our loss-of-function data that high levels of Klf9 in RGLs induce BMP4 expression and repress gene modules specifying mitogen signaling, fatty acid oxidation, RGL differentiation, and cell-cycle exit to inhibit RGL expansion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the loss-of-function experimental data.

claim: Klf9 acts as a transcriptional brake on RGL activation state and expansion through inhibition of symmetric self-renewal.
source: By combining conditional mouse genetics with in vivo clonal analysis and longitudinal two-photon imaging of RGLs, we demonstrated that Klf9 acts as a transcriptional brake on RGL activation state and expansion through inhibition of symmetric self-renewal (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple experimental approaches and is illustrated in Figure 5.

claim: Klf9 expression is higher in nondividing RGLs than in activated RGLs.
source: That Klf9 expression is higher in nondividing RGLs than in activated RGLs is consistent with gene expression profiling of quiescent adult hippocampal RGLs (Bottes et al., 2021; Knobloch et al., 2013; Jaeger and Jessberger, personal communication) and other quiescent somatic stem cells such as satellite cells (Pallafacchina et al., 2010) and NSCs in the subventricular zone (Codega et al., 2014; Morizur et al., 2018; Renault et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research and consistency with gene expression profiling studies.

claim: Loss of Klf9 in Gli1+ RGLs resulted in increased RGL activation.
source: Loss of Klf9 in Gli1+ RGLs resulted in increased RGL activation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from clonal analysis and translational profiling.

claim: Functional categories enriched among upregulated DEGs included phospholipase activity, mitogen growth factor signaling, and ligand-gated ion channels.
source: Functional categories enriched among upregulated DEGs (276) included phospholipase activity (Pla2g7, Pla2g4e, and Gpld1), mitogen growth factor signaling (Egfr, Fgfr3, Ntrk2, and Lfng), and ligand-gated ion channels (Gabra1, Chrna7, Grin2C, and P2r × 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis and gene ontology annotation.

claim: Loss of Klf9 in RGLs revealed elevation of metabolic programs sustaining energy production and lipogenesis through generation of Acetyl-CoA.
source: Additionally, our analysis revealed elevation of metabolic programs sustaining energy production and lipogenesis through generation of Acetyl-CoA: CoA- and fatty acid-ligase activity (Acsl3, Ascl6, Acss1, and Acsbg1) and oxidoreductase and aldehyde dehydrogenase activity (Acad12, Acox1, Ak1b10, Aldh3b1, and Aldh4a1) (Knobloch et al., 2013; Namba et al., 2021; Knobloch et al., 2017; Xie et al., 2016; Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis and gene ontology annotation.

claim: A complementary set of modules overrepresented in the downregulated gene set were quiescence growth factor signaling, extracellular matrix binding, cell adhesion, actin binding, TFs, and voltage-gate potassium channel activity.
source: A complementary set of modules overrepresented in the downregulated gene set (462 DEGs) were quiescence growth factor signaling (Bmp2 and Bmp4), extracellular matrix binding (Itga3, Itga10, and Igfbp3, 6, 7), cell adhesion (e.g., Emb, Itga3, and Itga5), actin binding (Iqgap1), TFs (NeuroD4 and Zic3), and voltage-gate potassium channel activity (Kcnj8 and Kcnq1) (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis and gene ontology annotation.

claim: Klf9 may activate BMP4 expression in RGLs to suppress activation in vivo.
source: Validation of specific DEGs in biochemically isolated transcripts from RGLs suggests that Klf9 may activate BMP4 expression in RGLs to suppress activation in vivo (Mira et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is inferred from validation data and supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Klf9 suppresses RGL proliferation through repression of mitogen signaling receptor tyrosine kinases (EGFR), lipidogenesis (Pla2g7), and cell cycle (CyclinA1).
source: Additionally, Klf9 suppresses RGL proliferation through repression of mitogen signaling receptor tyrosine kinases (EGFR), lipidogenesis (Pla2g7), and cell cycle (CyclinA1).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing upregulation of these genes upon Klf9 deletion.

claim: Pla2g7 is expressed only in RGLs and astrocytes in the DG and may represent a novel marker of activated RGLs.
source: Pla2g7, interestingly, is expressed only in RGLs and astrocytes in the DG (Shin et al., 2015; Hochgerner et al., 2018) and as such may represent a novel marker of activated RGLs.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research and inference from the current data.

claim: Lfng is exclusively expressed in RGLs, promotes Notch1 signaling through glycosylation of Notch1 and generation of NICD following ligand binding, and dictates RGL activation in a ligand-dependent manner.
source: Lfng is exclusively expressed in RGLs, promotes Notch1 signaling through glycosylation of Notch1 and generation of NICD following ligand binding, and dictates RGL activation in a ligand-dependent manner (Semerci et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Genetic overexpression of Lfng in T-cell progenitors sustained Notch1-mediated self-renewal and clonal expansion at expense of differentiation.
source: Genetic overexpression of Lfng in T-cell progenitors sustained Notch1-mediated self-renewal and clonal expansion at expense of differentiation (Yuan et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Enhanced fatty acid β-oxidation (FAO) is a metabolic program recruited to sustain RGL expansion.
source: Bioinformatics analysis of our data identified enhanced fatty acid β-oxidation (FAO), a substrate for energy production and lipogenesis as a metabolic program recruited to sustain RGL expansion (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is inferred from bioinformatics analysis of RNA-seq data and is illustrated in Figure 5.

claim: Inhibition of FAO resulted in a marked increase in symmetric differentiating divisions at expense of both symmetric and asymmetric self-renewal of NSCs in embryonic neocortical NSCs.
source: Specifically, inhibition of Tmlhe (a carnitine biosynthesis enzyme) and carnitine-dependent long-chain FAO (carnitine palmitoyltransferase I, CPT1, which catalyzes the rate-limiting reaction in this process) resulted in a marked increase in symmetric differentiating divisions at expense of both symmetric and asymmetric self-renewal of NSCs (Xie et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Inhibition of FAO prevented hematopoietic stem cell maintenance and promoted symmetric differentiating divisions of hematopoietic stem cells.
source: Inhibition of FAO prevented hematopoietic stem cell maintenance and promoted symmetric differentiating divisions of hematopoietic stem cells (Ito et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: High levels of FAO are directly linked to intestinal stemness.
source: High levels of FAO are directly linked to intestinal stemness (Mana et al., 2021) and persistence of proliferative capacity across cancers (Oren et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: NSCs require high levels of FAO for symmetric self-renewal or expansion.
source: Based on our data, we propose that NSCs, like other somatic stem cells and progenitors, require high levels of FAO for symmetric self-renewal or expansion.
evidence: The claim is a proposal based on the current data and comparison with other stem cell types.

claim: Klf9 corepresses a suite of genes associated with maintenance of RGLs in symmetric division mode.
source: We propose that Klf9 corepresses a suite of genes associated with maintenance of RGLs in symmetric division mode.
evidence: The claim is a proposal based on the experimental data.

claim: Notch signaling is implicated in sustaining symmetric divisions of neuroepithelial cells.
source: Pioneering studies have implicated Notch signaling in sustaining symmetric divisions of neuroepithelial cells (Egger et al., 2010), expansion of putative NSCs and progenitors (Androutsellis-Theotokis et al., 2006) and maintenance of radial glial cell like identity through inhibition of differentiation and cell-cycle exit (Gaiano et al., 2000; Yoon et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Genetic gain-of-function of Notch1 signaling in RGLs in the adult DG maintains RGLs at the expense of hippocampal neurogenesis.
source: Importantly, genetic gain-of-function of Notch1 signaling in RGLs in the adult DG maintains RGLs at the expense of hippocampal neurogenesis (Breunig et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: GABA(A) R signaling and PTEN signaling have been shown to promote quiescence and suppress RGL amplifying divisions.
source: To date, GABA(A) R signaling and PTEN signaling (by inhibiting PI3K–Akt pathway) have been shown to promote quiescence and suppress RGL amplifying divisions (Bonaguidi et al., 2011; Song et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Klf9 expression is regulated by steroid hormone signaling and neural activity.
source: Because Klf9 expression is regulated by steroid hormone signaling and neural activity (Scobie et al., 2009; Datson et al., 2011; Besnard et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Klf9 represses gene expression through recruitment of a mSin3A corepressor complex.
source: and Klf9 represses gene expression through recruitment of a mSin3A corepressor complex (Zhang et al., 2001)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The cell adhesion molecule Embigin regulates quiescence of hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells.
source: By way of example, candidate genes such as the cell adhesion molecule Embigin (downregulated DEG) regulates quiescence of hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (Silberstein et al., 2016)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The alpha7 nicotinic receptor (ChrnA7) has been shown to be required for maintaining RGL numbers.
source: whereas the alpha7 nicotinic receptor (upregulated DEG), ChrnA7, has been shown to be required for maintaining RGL numbers (Otto and Yakel, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Klf9 is enriched in other quiescent neural (SVZ) and somatic stem cell populations.
source: Fourth, our findings may guide investigation of functional significance of Klf9 enrichment in other quiescent neural (SVZ) (Codega et al., 2014; Morizur et al., 2018; Renault et al., 2009) and somatic stem cell populations (Pallafacchina et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Gli1CreERT2-labeled RGLs contribute to long-term maintenance and self-renewal.
source: We chose the Gli1CreERT2 driver line because population-based lineage tracing and chronic in vivo imaging suggests that Gli1CreERT2-labeled RGLs contribute to long-term maintenance and self-renewal (Ahn and Joyner, 2005; Bottes et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The recombination frequency of Klf9 was estimated to be approximately 32% in Gli1-positive tdTomato-labeled RGLs.
source: By analysis of Klf9 transcript-associated fluorescence intensity in Gli1-positive tdTomato-labeled RGLs we estimated the recombination frequency of Klf9 (i.e., reduction in Klf9-associated signal) to be approximately 32% in Gli1-positive tdTomato-labeled RGLs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and is illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Many of the multi-RGL containing clones also comprised of neural progenitors and astrocytes suggesting that loss of Klf9 biases RGL expansion but does not prevent RGL differentiation into progeny.
source: Many of the multi-RGL containing clones also comprised of neural progenitors and astrocytes suggesting that loss of Klf9 biases RGL expansion but does not prevent RGL differentiation into progeny (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is inferred from clonal analysis data and is illustrated in Figure 2D.

claim: Asymmetric divisions resulted in motile daughter cells that migrated away from their progenitors within one to two imaging sessions (3–6 days) and exhibited shorter and less stable processes.
source: As previously described (Pilz et al., 2018), asymmetric divisions resulted in motile daughter cells that migrated away from their progenitors within one to two imaging sessions (3–6 days) and exhibited shorter and less stable processes, often undergoing further divisions and differentiation (Figure 3B; Figure 3—video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and citation to prior research, and is illustrated in Figure 3B.

claim: Symmetric divisions resulted in the appearance of a faint radial process of a single static daughter cell that remained adjacent to its mother cell.
source: Conversely, and as shown previously (Pilz et al., 2018), symmetric divisions resulted in the appearance of a faint radial process of a single static daughter cell that remained adjacent to its mother cell (Figure 3B; Figure 3—videos 3; 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and citation to prior research, and is illustrated in Figure 3B.

claim: Analysis of Klf9 levels by qRT-PCR suggests greater than 50% recombination efficiency of Klf9 in targeted cell populations.
source: Analysis of Klf9 levels by qRT-PCR suggests greater than 50% recombination efficiency of Klf9 in targeted cell populations.
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data.

claim: Klf9 functions as an activator or repressor depending on cellular context, although repression appears to be the dominant mode of gene regulation.
source: Our genome-wide expression analysis suggests that Klf9 functions as an activator or repressor depending on cellular context, although repression appears to be the dominant mode of gene regulation (Knoedler et al., 2017; Ying et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is inferred from genome-wide expression analysis and supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Lineage tracing studies on embryonic neocortical NSCs have demonstrated a role for FAO in maintenance of NSC identity and proliferation.
source: In fact, lineage tracing studies on embryonic neocortical NSCs have demonstrated a role for FAO in maintenance of NSC identity and proliferation (Namba et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Deletion of Cpt1a (and inhibition of FAO) in adult hippocampal NSC and progenitors impaired expansion and reduced numbers of RGLs.
source: Specifically, deletion of Cpt1a (and inhibition of FAO) in adult hippocampal NSC and progenitors impaired expansion and reduced numbers of RGLs. However, it could not be determined if this was due to death and/or inhibition of symmetric self-renewal of RGLs (Knobloch et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Klf9 may directly suppress a proneurogenic program in RGLs (e.g., NeuroD4).
source: Klf9 may also directly suppress a proneurogenic program in RGLs (e.g., NeuroD4, downregulated DEG, Supplementary file 3; Masserdotti et al., 2015)
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data showing NeuroD4 as a downregulated DEG and supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Akt-dependent regulation of NSC activation through inactivation of FoxO3 may require Klf9 downregulation.
source: Klf9 expression is reduced in NSCs lacking FoxO3 (Renault et al., 2009). Thus, Akt-dependent regulation of NSC activation through inactivation of FoxO3 (Urbán et al., 2019) may require Klf9 downregulation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the relationship between FoxO3 and Klf9 expression and supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Klf9 expression is reduced in NSCs lacking FoxO3.
source: Klf9 expression is reduced in NSCs lacking FoxO3 (Renault et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Inhibition of pulsatile glucocorticoid receptor signaling has been shown to promote RGL quiescence.
source: Inhibition of pulsatile glucocorticoid receptor signaling has also been shown to promote RGL quiescence (Schouten et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Klf9 may support an epigenetic mechanism for reversible, experiential regulation of NSC decision making.
source: Because Klf9 expression is regulated by steroid hormone signaling and neural activity (Scobie et al., 2009; Datson et al., 2011; Besnard et al., 2018) and Klf9 represses gene expression through recruitment of a mSin3A corepressor complex (Zhang et al., 2001), Klf9 may support an epigenetic mechanism for reversible, experiential regulation of NSC decision making.
evidence: The claim is speculative and inferred from the properties of Klf9 and supported by citations to prior research.
